concept.name: Lending protocol
concept.definition: A lending protocol is a set of smart contracts (e.g. Aave, Compound) that pools supplied assets and lets borrowers draw loans against deposited collateral, with interest rates, collateral requirements and liquidations enforced automatically by code.
concept.intuition: It is a pawnshop run by a robot: depositors earn interest, borrowers post more collateral than they take, and the robot seizes and sells the collateral the moment the loan turns unsafe.
concept.mechanics: Suppliers deposit assets into pools and receive interest-bearing receipts (e.g. aTokens); borrowers post collateral and borrow up to an asset-specific LTV, paying a utilization-driven interest rate that accrues algorithmically. Oracles price collateral continuously, and when a position's health factor falls below 1, any third party can liquidate it for a bonus.
concept.failure_modes: Oracle failure or manipulation can trigger wrongful liquidations or let attackers borrow against worthless collateral; fast crashes can outrun liquidators and leave the protocol with bad debt; smart contract exploits and governance parameter mistakes are systemic risks.
concept.misconceptions: DeFi lending is not peer-to-peer matching — lenders face the pool, and borrowers face the protocol, with rates set by utilization curves. Deposit insurance does not exist; 'safe' yields embed smart contract, oracle and liquidation risk.
concept.example: A user supplies $10,000 of ETH to Aave (80% liquidation threshold) and borrows $6,000 of a stablecoin; interest accrues to suppliers from the borrower's rate, and if ETH falls enough that the health factor crosses 1, liquidators repay part of the debt and seize discounted ETH.
